_comment: content-review replies: the AI content check's stage 2 (#1037, src/content_check/review.rs). One request per course with parts Jev scored high; the reply is the verdict JSON. The key is a [fixture:NAME] token in the course text (default: 'default', a fine verdict). 'harmful' quotes the stand-in Jev's self-harm phrase, 'harmful-new' its hate phrase and says the override note doesn't cover it. See docs/testing.md.

reply.report: The word that scored high is taught as ordinary vocabulary in a neutral example. Nothing in the lesson targets anyone.

reply.question: self_harm
reply.report: The lesson tells learners that hurting themselves is the answer when things hurt. That encourages self-harm, and nothing around it frames it as something to avoid or points to help.

reply.question: hate
reply.report: A new lesson calls a group of people vermin, which is hate speech. The override note was considered: it covers the earlier passage only, not this new text.
